facts.fact: Jurist Abdou Malam Garba told Le Sahel that Niger has no AI-specific framework but Law 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data applies to AI and obliges AI developers and service providers operating in Niger to declare to the HAPDP.
Per the same jurist, the HAPDP is the body before which AI developers, makers and service providers operating in Niger must file a declaration under Law 2022-59.

NER.note: Nothing on a government body using an AI system.

facts.fact: Jurist Abdou Malam Garba said Niger has no specific AI framework, but Law 2022-59 specifically obliges AI developers, makers and service providers operating in Niger to declare to the HAPDP.

NER.note: Nothing on an AI tool in a public sector system.
Nothing on AI built or hosted in Niger.

facts.fact: Jurist Abdou Malam Garba cites Niger's law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection as governing data processing.
The same jurist says the law requires AI developers and providers to declare to the HAPDP, the data protection authority.

NER.note: A jurist calls digital sovereignty necessary; no strategy or rule on state data is stated.
Only a suggestion to use open data; no publishing body is named.
Only a hope that a legal framework will help startups; no startup law or fund is stated.
No hub or incubator is named.
